landing.metaTitle: LiftPilot — lift design and geared machine checks
landing.metaDescription: Lift design software: shaft survey from DXF/DWG, drawing sets, 3D simulation, geared machine sizing and checks, and the calculation report.
landing.h1: Lift design and geared machine checks
landing.answer: LiftPilot is the software for anyone replacing or modernising a lift: from the shaft survey in DXF or DWG to a design run through the UNI EN 81-20 and 81-50 checks the software computes, with the machine chosen, the 3D simulation and the draft drawing set and calculation report to check and sign.
landing.status: Results are drafts to be checked and signed by a qualified technician; every value the software uses has its source and status in the standards register, and those still to be checked are marked ⚠.
landing.betaFree: Free during the beta, with every function and unlimited colleagues.
landing.heroChecks: Example A, computed now by engine {engine}
landing.machineAlt: Geared machine on its bedplate: motor with cooling fins, drum brake with electromagnet, worm gearbox, handwheel for emergency operation and traction sheave with four ropes.
landing.machineCaption: The machine of the calculator’s example A: sheave D 560 mm, 4 ropes Ø 10 mm, ratio 1:43, 7.5 kW motor. Illustrative model, not a real product.

landing.who2Text: Shaft, section and machine room with editable dimensions and DXF and DWG export.
landing.who3Text: Checks of the existing installation with the ropes in place, compared with the new machine.
landing.trustTitle: Security and control of the data
landing.t1Text: Servers in the EU; a company’s projects are visible to its own users only.
landing.t2Text: DXF and DWG are read in the browser: only the measurements and the file’s fingerprint reach the server.
landing.t3Text: Calculations, designs and drawing sets are saved with the engine version and a SHA‑256 fingerprint; a variant is a new record.
landing.t4Text: Distinct roles — owner, design engineer, sales, technician — with different permissions, passwords protected with Argon2id, an activity log.
landing.normsTitle: Which standards is it based on?
landing.normsLead: The software’s Italian standards profile covers:
landing.normsNote: Profile {profile}. Every value the software uses is tied to a document, clause and status in the standards register; the ⚠ sign marks estimates, the software’s choices and values still to be checked against the text in force.
landing.faq1a: Yes. Besides selecting and checking the machine, LiftPilot helps design the shaft, the section with pit and headroom and the machine room, and prepares drafts of the drawing set, the calculation report and the DXF and DWG drawings, to be checked and signed.
landing.faq2q: Which CAD files can I use?
landing.faq2a: DXF and DWG. The drawing opens in the browser and is not uploaded to the server: you measure the shaft with one click. Dimensions can also be entered by hand.
landing.faq3q: Can I export the saved project?
landing.faq3a: Yes: the drawing set as PDF, every view as DXF and DWG in millimetres at full size, and the calculation report as PDF.
landing.faq4q: Does LiftPilot replace the report signed by the engineer?
landing.faq4a: No. LiftPilot prepares the calculations and the report; the document becomes a calculation report when a qualified engineer checks and signs it, and the responsibility stays theirs.
landing.faq5q: Does it work with the machine at the bottom?
landing.faq5a: Yes. The calculation follows the rope path for a machine on top with direct pull, on top with a diverting pulley, and at the bottom with two head pulleys, including the upward load on the shaft.
landing.faq6q: Can I keep the existing ropes in a replacement?
landing.faq6a: Yes, it is the default: the new ropes have the same number and diameter as those fitted, and the proposal keeps them too.
landing.faq7a: On servers in the European Union. A company’s projects are visible only to users of the same company.
landing.faq8a: The interface is in Italian, English and Bulgarian; the calculation report and the drawing sets are in Italian.
landing.endTitle: Bring your next installation to LiftPilot
landing.endText: Register your company and confirm the email address: you can create the first project right away and invite your colleagues.

lift.rif_hint: The existing car frame stays: by practice the job remains a modification of the lift (DPR 162/1999, art. 2) and is tested to UNI 10411, not as a new installation. Every part but the car frame is ticked: untick those that stay and add rated speed, rated load or travel if they change. A complete replacement, car frame included, is tested as a new installation (UNI EN 81-20/50).

lift.var_down: A load decreases: the checks of the load enter the result (buffers, progressive safety gear).

lift.sum_ride: From {from} to {to} with {load} kg: T1/T2 reaches at most {util} of the braking traction limit; motor torque up to {torque} N·m.
lift.sum_ride_over: From {from} to {to} with {load} kg: during the ride T1/T2 exceeds the braking traction limit ({util}); with the conventional friction the ropes would slip. Reduce the design acceleration or increase the traction (groove, wrap angle). Motor torque up to {torque} N·m.
lift.sum_brake_ok: The brake decelerates the car at {a} m/s²: T1/T2 reaches {util} of the limit and the ropes hold. Stop in {d0} cm.
lift.sum_brake_slip: The brake decelerates at {a} m/s²: T1/T2 asks {util} times the traction available and the ropes slip on the sheave. The car stops in {d1} cm instead of {d0} cm.
lift.sum_brake_runaway: The brake decelerates at {a} m/s², but T1/T2 passes the traction even with the car at rest: the ropes slip and the car runs on to the buffers.
lift.sum_brake_none: The brake does not stop the car: its torque ({tb} N·m) cannot hold it and the car runs on to the buffers.
lift.sum_brake_min: On its own the brake would decelerate at {a0} m/s²: the check uses the standard’s minimum, {a} m/s².
lift.sum_loading_ok: With 1.25 times the rated load T1/T2 reaches {util} of the limit: the ropes hold and the car stays at the floor.
lift.sum_loading_fail: While loading T1/T2 passes the limit ({util}): the ropes slip and the car sinks with the doors open.
lift.sum_stall_ok: With the counterweight on its buffers T1/T2 reaches {efa} ({ratio}): the ropes slip and the car is not lifted.
lift.sum_stall_fail: With the counterweight on its buffers T1/T2 stays at {ratio} against {efa}: the ropes do not slip and the car is lifted toward the ceiling.
lift.sum_buffer_ok: Impact at 1.15 times the rated speed: the buffer compresses by {x} mm of {stroke} mm; peak deceleration {g} g, indicative (linear model): the limits hold by type, from the supplier’s certificate.
lift.sum_buffer_fail: Impact at 1.15 times the rated speed: the stroke of {stroke} mm is not enough and the buffer goes solid.

legal.dataTitle: What data do we process, and why?

For the owner they are needed to enter into and perform the contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR): without them the account cannot be created.

Colleagues: the owner invites a colleague by entering their name, e-mail and role (Art. 14 GDPR); the account exists only once the colleague opens the invitation’s link and chooses their own password, and an invitation not accepted expires after {inviteDays} days. We process the data of their account as controller, to secure sign-in and the service, in our and the company’s legitimate interest in giving its people access (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR); whom to invite and with which role is decided by the company, which is the controller for that and we its processor (Art. {dpa}).

Subscription: the identifiers of the customer and of the subscription at Stripe, its status, the pack of slots and the end of the paid period. You enter the billing data (name, address, VAT number, e-mail) in Stripe’s payment; card data never reach LiftPilot. Basis: the contract and tax obligations (Art. 6(1)(b) and (c) GDPR).

Activity log: who in your company did what and when (sign-ins, saved calculations, issued drawing sets, changed prices and subscription, accepted terms, exported data), for security and the traceability of technical documents (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR, legitimate interest).

E-mails and correspondence: the address confirmation, the colleagues’ invitations, the links for a new password and the notices these terms provide for (changes of the terms, deletion of an inactive company); the messages you write to us, to answer them (Art. 6(1)(b) and (f) GDPR). The e-mails carry no tracking pixels or tracked links.

Security: the IP address is used, in memory only, to limit repeated attempts, and the application does not store it; the web server’s logs (IP address, page, time, browser) protect the service from abuse (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

We do not process any data on the basis of consent.

Manufacturers’ data come from their documents, with the source shown, and must be confirmed on the data sheet and in the quotation before ordering. LiftPilot does not replace the standards, the technician’s judgement, on-site tests or the checks of the notified body.

The contract is concluded when the owner, having accepted these terms in the registration form, confirms their e-mail address; the paid subscription when Stripe confirms the first payment. All the data entered can be corrected before the form is sent.

We keep every version of these terms and, for each company, the version accepted with its date, the confirmations given and the SHA-256 fingerprint of the text. The company uses the service for its own technical work and does not upload illegal content, data or material it has no rights to, or malicious code. Companies’ content is not public: we do not check it in advance or with automated systems, and we act on a notice or for security.

Anyone can report content they consider illegal to info@carbonstealth.eu, stating the reason, the exact location of the content, their name and e-mail (save where the law provides otherwise) and a statement of good faith. We confirm receipt, a person decides, and we communicate the decision with the means of redress.

If we restrict content or suspend or close an account, we tell the company with a statement of reasons — the facts, the rule applied and the means of redress: review, by writing to info@carbonstealth.eu, and the courts —, unless the law or an authority prevents it.

legal.dpaTitle: Processing of data on behalf of the company (Art. 28 GDPR)
legal.dpaText:
For the personal data the company enters (installations, calculations, drawing sets, order drafts, price list, colleagues’ invitations and roles) the company is the controller and Carbon Stealth VCC the processor (Art. 28 GDPR); this article is the agreement between them.

Subject matter and duration: the provision of the service, for the term of the contract and of the data retrieval period (Art. {exit}). Nature and purpose: storage, consultation, calculation, generation of documents and service e-mails, only to provide the service. Types of data: users’ names, e-mails and roles; names of clients, owners or building managers, installations’ addresses and serial numbers, logos and the other data the company chooses to enter; the company does not enter special categories of data (Art. 9 GDPR). Data subjects: the company’s users, its clients and principals, building owners and managers.

We process the data only on the company’s documented instructions — these terms and its use of the service’s functions —, including with regard to transfers to third countries: we keep the data in the European Union, and a sub-processor processes them outside the EEA only with the safeguards of Arts. 44–46 GDPR (an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses); obligations under Union or Member State law remain, in which case we inform the company beforehand where the law allows. If we believe an instruction infringes the GDPR, we say so at once. Whoever processes the data for us is bound to confidentiality. Security measures (Art. 32 GDPR): servers in Germany, encrypted connections (TLS), passwords only as Argon2id hashes, access by role within the company and separated between companies, activity log, backups kept for {backupDays} days.

Sub-processors authorised in general: Hetzner Online GmbH (Germany, servers in Nuremberg) and Sendinblue SAS — Brevo (France, service e-mails). Any addition or replacement is notified to the owner by e-mail at least 30 days in advance: the company may object on data protection grounds and, if no solution is found, terminate without cost before the change. We impose on sub-processors data protection obligations equivalent to these and remain liable to the company for their performance.

We assist the company, with appropriate measures, in answering data subjects’ requests and in complying with Arts. 32–36 GDPR as far as we are concerned, and we notify it of a personal data breach without undue delay after becoming aware of it. At the end of the contract, at the company’s choice, we return the data through the service’s exports and then delete them, unless the law requires them to be kept; they disappear from the backups within {backupDays} days. We make available the information needed to demonstrate compliance with this article and allow for audits, including inspections, by the company or an auditor it mandates who is bound to confidentiality, on reasonable notice.
legal.exitTitle: Cancellation, switching provider and return of data
legal.exitText:
The company can cancel at any time, also to switch to another provider or to its own systems; cancelling the subscription takes effect at the end of the period already paid. Switching needs no notice and costs nothing: it starts from the request and the transition lasts at most 30 days, during which the contract keeps applying and we assist the company and the third parties it authorises, maintain the service, point out the known risks to its continuity and protect the data, in transfer too.

The owner downloads the company’s data themselves for as long as the account exists and in any case for at least 30 days after the end of the transition or of the subscription: reports, drawing sets and projects in PDF, DXF and DWG and, from the Company page, all the data entered and the records in a structured, machine-readable format (JSON). The documents of a record the current version of the software no longer reproduces (“to update”) are downloaded after making the record again with one click, read-only too, except when the data entered must be corrected in the form; the data entered and the results of every record are always in the JSON file. The full list of the exportable data, the formats, the export interface and the jurisdiction of our servers are on the page “Data and formats” (https://liftpilot.carbonstealth.eu/en/data), which we keep up to date (Arts. 25, 26, 28 and 30 of Regulation (EU) 2023/2854, the Data Act). The software’s catalogue data, standards register and calculation engines cannot be exported (Art. {license}), nor can the accounts’ security data (password hashes, access links, sessions).

The contract is considered terminated, and we confirm it to the owner by e-mail, when the owner tells us that the switch is complete or that they do not wish to switch but to have the data erased. From then on the data stay downloadable, read-only, for as long as the account exists: we delete it with all the company’s data within 30 days of the owner’s request to info@carbonstealth.eu, except the data the law requires us to keep, and confirm it by e-mail; or for inactivity, as the privacy notice states. dataPage.title: Data, formats and jurisdiction
dataPage.metaDescription: Which data a company can download from LiftPilot, in which formats, how the JSON file is built, how to switch provider and where the servers are (Data Act).
dataPage.keywords: LiftPilot Data Act, JSON data export, SaaS data portability, cloud provider switching, server jurisdiction Germany, Carbon Stealth
dataPage.lead: The information Regulation (EU) 2023/2854 (the Data Act) asks of a service like LiftPilot: the data a company can take with it and in which formats, how to switch provider, where the servers are and how we protect them from access by third-country authorities. The terms of use refer to this page (Art. {exit}).
dataPage.filesTitle: Which data can be downloaded, and in which format?
dataPage.filesText: Everything the company entered or generated, for as long as the account exists and for at least 30 days after the subscription ends, at no cost:

reports.what: Calculation reports and technical reports, issued drawing sets, projects

order.format: PDF and DOCX (Office Open XML, ISO/IEC 29500)

drawings.what: Drawings of the shaft and of the project
drawings.format: DXF (AutoCAD 2007 version, AC1021) and DWG (AutoCAD 2000 version, AC1015)

dataPage.jsonTitle: How is the company’s JSON file built?
dataPage.jsonText:
One JSON document (RFC 8259, UTF-8 encoding): format “{format}”, version {version}. Amounts in euro cents without VAT, lengths in millimetres unless stated, dates and times in ISO 8601 (UTC), images in base64. The identifiers (id) link the entries to one another; a new or changed field raises the version, and this page says so.

The top-level keys:

keys.format: The name of the format: always “{format}”.
keys.termsVersion: The version of the terms of use published when the file was created; the one each user accepted is in users.
keys.note: A note on the units of measurement.
keys.company: The company: name, VAT number, city, state of the subscription and of the trial.
keys.users: The users: name, e-mail, role, language, dates of creation, last sign-in, address confirmation and acceptance of the terms; never the passwords or the links.
keys.invites: The waiting invitations: e-mail, name, role, expiry.
keys.logos: The company’s logos, with SHA-256 fingerprint and size.
keys.projects: The projects, each with its records (below).
keys.priceItems: The company’s price list: the price of each article of the catalogues.
keys.customPrices: The free lines of the price list, with text, price and quantity basis.
keys.auditLog: The activity log: who, what, when.

dataPage.projectText: Each project holds its records, each with the data entered, the engine version, the results and the SHA-256 fingerprint that guarantees its integrity:

project.calculations: the machine calculations, with the internal reviews
project.roomDesigns: the surveys of the machine room
project.drawingSets: the issued drawing sets, with the revisions and the PDF’s fingerprint
project.formDrafts: the drafts of the forms not saved yet

dataPage.excludedText: The data that belong to the software, not to the company: the manufacturers’ catalogues, the standards register and the calculation engines (Art. {license} of the terms of use). And the security data: password hashes, access links and sessions.
dataPage.switchTitle: How do you switch to another provider?
dataPage.switchText:
The company cancels at any time from “Payment, invoices and cancellation”, effective at the end of the period already paid. Switching needs no notice and costs nothing: it starts from the request, the transition lasts at most 30 days and during it, on request to {email}, we assist the company and the third parties it authorises. The data can be downloaded for as long as the account exists and for at least 30 days after the subscription ends.

The contract is considered terminated when the owner tells us that the switch is complete or that they want the data erased, and we confirm it by e-mail. At the owner’s request we delete the company and all its data within 30 days and confirm it by e-mail; they disappear from the backups within the following {backupDays} days. Only the data the law requires us to keep, such as invoices, remain.
dataPage.whereTitle: Where are the data, and under which jurisdiction?
dataPage.whereText:
The server and the backups are at {host}, in the Nuremberg data centre in Germany: the infrastructure is subject to European Union law and German law. Carbon Stealth VCC, which provides the service, is a Bulgarian company subject to European Union law and Bulgarian law.

The service e-mails go through Sendinblue SAS (Brevo, France), the subscription payments through Stripe Payments Europe, Limited (Ireland). Transfers outside the European Economic Area and their safeguards are described in the privacy notice.
dataPage.accessTitle: How do we protect the data from access by third-country authorities?
dataPage.accessText:
Technical measures: the service, the servers and the backups are in the European Union, data travel encrypted (TLS) and each company sees only its own. Contractual measures: {host}, which holds the data, is a German company bound by an agreement under Art. 28 GDPR to process them only on our instructions. Organisational measures: every request by a third-country authority is examined by our legal representative in the light of Art. 32 of the Data Act and recorded with the answer given.

We act on such a request for the company’s non-personal data only in the cases of Art. 32 — an international agreement or, failing one, the safeguards the same article requires —, we provide only the minimum data needed and we tell the company before acting on the request, unless it serves law enforcement purposes and for as long as that is necessary.
dataPage.contactText: Carbon Stealth VCC, {email}, phone {phoneBg} (Bulgaria) and {phoneIt} (Italy), in Italian, English or Bulgarian.
dataPage.filesNote: The documents of a record the current version of the software no longer reproduces (“to update”) are downloaded after making the record again with one click, read-only too, except when the data entered must be corrected in the form; the data entered and the results of every record are always in the JSON file. Issued drawing sets are downloaded as the PDF kept after their issue.

dataPage.apiTitle: Is there an interface for the export?
dataPage.apiText: Yes, free of charge and the same for every company: a GET request to {base}/api/company/export returns the JSON file described above to the signed-in owner. It is the same request as the button on the Company page, at most 6 times an hour per company. The new provider receives the file from the owner; this page describes the format, to write the program that reads it (Art. 30(2) of the Data Act).

pricing.answerPrice: LiftPilot costs {base} {per} for the company’s owner; colleagues are added with a pack of 5, 10 or unlimited slots, and a new company gets a {days}-day free trial, with no credit card.

pricing.trialText: Yes: a new company gets a {days}-day free trial from its first sign-in, with every function for the owner and no credit card. pricing.faq2a: Through Stripe, in advance for each period; the invoice carries the billing details entered in the payment. LiftPilot never sees or keeps the card details.
pricing.faq3a: At any time from “Payment, invoices and cancellation”: the subscription stays active until the end of the period already paid, with no refund of the unused part, and the data stay downloadable.
pricing.faq4a: Yes, with an e-mail to the owner at least 30 days before the renewal it applies from: whoever does not accept it can cancel before.
